newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Competition for Ostend airport ground handling.
newsitem.headline: Competition for Ostend airport ground handling.

text.p: Companies are lining up to become the second freight handling company at Ostend, an airport spokesman said.
Two Dutch companies, Maastricht Handling and Aero Groundservices, and UK-based Servisair Plc have so far approached the airport as potential candidates, he told Reuters.
Ostend is in the process of building a new freight handling area able to cope with an additional 150,000 tonnes annual capacity. It now handles around 90,000 tonnes a year of flown airfreight.
The taxiway is already completed with work now taking place on the apron. "If everything goes to schedule the cargo village and business park should be ready by this time next year," he said.
"This area will be exclusively reserved for cargo and aircraft maintenance," he said.
Cargo handling is at present carried out exclusively by Belgavia at the moment but at end-1997 a European Commission ruling will disallow monopoly handling at European airports.

Some older and noisier aircraft now flying into the Netherlands -- where there are increasingly tough operational and environmental rules -- may switch to Ostend and the Dutch companies who provide their existing groundhandling services are expected to want to follow them to the Belgian airport, industry sources said.
